--------
Former Mexican Mafia member Ramon “Mundo” Mendoza sits down with Vlad to discuss the brutal loyalty codes that ruled his life, including whether he would have carried out an order against his own brother, Angel. Mendoza recalls Joe Morgan attempting to sponsor Angel into the organization after a hit involving a Black Guerilla Family member, and explains why he blocked the move to spare their mother from heartbreak.

The conversation also covers Mendoza’s Kern County arrest, his time in Southern California awaiting U.S. Marshals protection, an ex-con with a gun charge, and why he still hides his face decades after leaving prison. Vlad connects Mendoza’s story to witness protection, Alpo Martinez of Harlem and Paid in Full, and the Tupac murder case in Las Vegas. Now 76, Mendoza speaks on faith, law enforcement training, redemption, and the lasting cost of gang life.

--------
In this VladTV interview, Rex Holloway recounts his journey from a gifted kid in East Texas near Houston to juvenile detention, armed robberies, and a 10-year Texas prison sentence at 17. Holloway details the harsh realities of TDCJ life, the Texas Youth Commission, Huntsville intake, Ferguson Unit, solitary confinement, prison politics, and how he rose within the Aryan Brotherhood of Texas (ABT) before walking away after five years.

He breaks down the difference between the Aryan Brotherhood of Texas and California’s AB, the impact of the Ruiz lawsuit, conflicts involving Aryan Circle, Texas Syndicate, and Mexican Mafia politics, and the mental toll of years in administrative segregation. Holloway also discusses reading about John Gotti and Sammy “The Bull” Gravano, rebuilding his life after release, staying free for 21 years, and finding success, marriage, and perspective beyond prison.
